title: Typhoons During the Last 25 Years
caption_extra: Since '84 typhoons have visited Japan seventeen times, mentioning only those cases when the atmospheric pressure fell to 720 m.m. or below. These typhoons are tablated as follows:—

rows: Came from off Shikoku and devastated Hamamatsu, Suruga, Tōtōmi, Musashi, Hitachi, etc.
Came from Luchu, and traversed Hokuroku, and O-u districts.
Came from Luchu, and traversed Ise, Mino, Owari, Shinano, Echigo, reaching southern parts of Hokkaido.
Came from Manchuria and emerged at Pacific via middle Hokkaido.
Came from Luchu and touched northern part of Kyushu.
Came from Oshima, Kagoshima; and visited Nagasaki, turned eastward in southern part of Japan Sea, and emerged in Pacific Ocean after crossing Echigo and O-u.
Crossed Kyushu south to north, advanced northeasterly in Japan Sea, to reath Hokkaido.
Came from Eastern Sea, China, passed Formosa, Kyushu, Sanyo, and San-in districts, to advance to northern part of Hokkaido via Japan Sea.
Cut across Shikoku and western Honshu, to proceed to Manchuria.
Reached Honshu at Kii, and entered Japan Sea via Kyoto-Osaka districts.
Ran northeasterly off Kii, landed near Hamamatsu, and after devastating Pacific side of middle Honshu, reached eastern part of Hokkaido.
Landed at southern extremity of Kyushu, to run across eastern half of the island, and to enter Japan Sea via Suwo.
Came from south of Luchu archipelago, entered Eastern Sea, China; entered Japan Sea via Korean strait, and enter Pacific Ocean.
Came from between Formosa and Luchu archipelago, cut across northern Kyushu, entered Island Sea, and emerged at Japan Sea via Okayama and Tajima.
Came from south of Luchu archipelago, advanced northeasterly to reach Korea and finally Siberian coast.
Came from south of Luchu, passed Korean strait, turned easterly in O-u districts, to enter Pacific Ocean.
Came from south of Luchu, archipelago, turned easterly at Oshima, off Izu, and proceeded northeasterly via Hachijo island.
